title: Could we build Iron Man's arc reactor?
grammar_focus: could / would for imagined and impossible situations

instructions.text: Why can't we just make a nuclear reactor small enough to wear? Check what the speaker really says.

content.paragraph: Put the speaker's points in the order he makes them.
wordBank: He says the arc reactor is fictional
He says it would destroy your body
He asks why we can't make reactors smaller
He admits he loves Iron Man
He explains the driver energy problem
correctAnswers: He asks why we can't make reactors smaller
He admits he loves Iron Man
He says the arc reactor is fictional
He explains the driver energy problem
He says it would destroy your body

content.question: Why does the speaker say he wishes he could fly?
options: To show he likes the film before he criticises it
Because he builds flying suits for his job
To prove that the arc reactor is real
content.correctAnswer: To show he likes the film before he criticises it

instructions.text: Which sentence would the speaker agree with? Click one.

words.text: Fusion needs too much energy in too small a space.
words.feedback: Yes. That's his main point: you can't put enough driver energy into a space small enough to wear.

words.text: Nuclear reactors haven't been invented yet.
words.feedback: No. He says we have already invented nuclear reactors. The problem is making them small.

words.text: The arc reactor works, but it's too expensive.
words.feedback: No. He never talks about money. He says the arc reactor is fictional.

words.text: Scientists will make a small one very soon.
words.feedback: No. He says you could never do it in a space small enough to fit on a body.

keyWords: Fusion needs too much energy in too small a space.

pairs.right: it wouldn't fit on a body

columns: Why it's impossible on a body

blanks: it can't fit in a tiny space

tokens: it can't fit in a tiny space

content.template: You could never put enough energy into a space small enough to _____ on a human body.

content.question: According to the speaker, could a real arc reactor be built?
options: No. It's fictional, and it could never fit safely on a body.
Yes, but it would be very expensive.
Only if it was used for flying.
content.correctAnswer: No. It's fictional, and it could never fit safely on a body.

instructions.text: Many words in the video have more than one meaning. Choose the meaning the speaker is using.

content.question: "...large amounts of driver energy..." What does driver mean here?
options: A person who drives a vehicle
A type of fuel burned inside a reactor
Something that starts or pushes a process forward
Software that lets a computer use a device
A musical instrument used in films
content.correctAnswer: Something that starts or pushes a process forward

content.question: "...into a very small space..." What does space mean here?
options: The empty part inside an atom
An amount of room or area
content.correctAnswer: An amount of room or area

content.question: "The major challenge with fusion reactors..." What does major mean here?
options: A student's main subject at university
Happening in the month of May

content.question: "...cooling the reactor parts and also shielding." What does shielding mean here?
options: A metal case that keeps the reactor warm
Material that protects people from something dangerous
content.correctAnswer: Material that protects people from something dangerous

content.question: "...create these fusion conditions..." What does conditions mean here?
options: The exact situation needed for something to happen
Something you put in your hair after shampoo
content.correctAnswer: The exact situation needed for something to happen

content.question: "Iron Man uses an arc reactor..." What does arc mean here?
options: A curved line, like part of a circle
How a story develops from start to end
A bright flow of electricity between two points
content.correctAnswer: A bright flow of electricity between two points

instructions.text: Can and will talk about what is real. Could and would talk about what is imagined or impossible.
I wish I could fly. It would destroy your body. You could never do that.

content.template: As much as I love Iron Man, I wish that I myself _____ fly.
I can't speak Chinese. I wish I _____ Chinese.

content.question: "It would destroy your body." What does would do in this sentence?
options: It talks about a past habit
It says the future is certain

content.question: "You could never fit it on a body." What does this mean?
options: It was possible in the past
You aren't allowed to do it

pairs.right: a reaction to happen near your chest.

instructions.text: The speaker says "there's all the other things". Which sentence is correct in formal writing? Click one.

words.feedback: This is normal in speech (the speaker says it), but in writing use "there are" with a plural.

words.text: There are all the other things.
words.feedback: Correct. In writing, use "there are" with a plural noun. In speech, many people say "there's".

words.text: There is all the other thing.
words.feedback: No. "All the other" needs a plural: "things".

keyWords: There are all the other things.
